basics.name: George Webber
basics.summary: Fourth-year PhD researcher at King’s College London developing computational methods for generative modelling, inverse problems and probabilistic machine learning, with applications to medical image reconstruction. Research interests include measurement conditioning, efficient conditional sampling, statistical data consistency, and the effects of learned priors and model mismatch. First-Class MMathCompSci from the University of Oxford. Expected PhD submission: September 2027.

volunteer.summary: Co-instructor of Medical Image Reconstruction: from Foundations to AI with Andrew Reader and Siqi Li (10 November); co-chair of Advanced Tomographic Reconstruction Techniques (2) with Jinyi Qi (14 November).
ICLR; Nature Communications; Medical Image Analysis; IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging; IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging; Pattern Recognition; and other journals.

courses: Project: Fully Bayesian 3D PET-MR Neuroimaging Reconstruction.

Developing diffusion- and flow-based methods for inverse problems, including measurement conditioning, efficient sampling and optimisation-based guidance. Investigating statistical consistency and the effects of model mismatch and learned priors on reconstruction.
Supervisors: Prof. Andrew J. Reader and Prof. Andrew P. King.
